name: Museum der Wahrnehmung
kurzbeschreibung: The interactive World of Senses in Sölden: sensory stations, optical phenomena, and high-alpine perceptions in the rear Ötztal.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Interactive Exhibition of Perception and the Senses in Sölden in the Tyrolean Ötztal valley offers visitors an engaging and educational interplay of sensory physiology, physical natural phenomena, and high-alpine perception. Located at over 1,350 metres above sea level in the vibrant centre of Sölden, this modern exhibition invites children, youths, and adults to test their senses – sight, hearing, touch, balance, and spatial orientation – through hands-on experiments and to perceive the familiar world from surprising new perspectives.

Interactive Stations & Sensory Phenomena

At the heart of the exhibition are more than 60 thoughtfully crafted interactive and experimental discovery stations. Visitors navigate captivating mirror mazes with endless reflections, explore bewildering optical illusions that challenge human vision, and experiment with acoustic resonance in whisper galleries and sound chambers. Tactile columns and dynamic balance courses challenge motor coordination and demonstrate vividly how the human brain processes and filters complex sensory stimuli. A unique thematic focus is dedicated to perception in the high mountains: How do colours, sound waves, scents, and oxygen levels change in the thin air above 3,000-metre summits? What remarkable sensory capabilities allow alpine wildlife such as ibexes, chamois, and golden eagles to thrive in sheer cliff environments? Being completely indoors and weather-independent, the exhibition is an ideal excursion destination for families combining playful learning with unforgettable discoveries.

Visit & Arrival

The interactive exhibition is open year-round during both summer and winter tourist seasons: daily from 10:00 to 18:00 (last admission at 17:00). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): Adults approx. €12.00, children and youths approx. €7.50, family passes from €26.00. Holders of the Ötztal Inside Summer Card receive reduced or free entry. Arrival by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12, exit Ötztal, then follow the B186 (Ötztalstraße) approximately 35 kilometres up the valley directly to Sölden; parking garages are located at Gaislachkogl and Zentrum. By public transport: Rail (ÖBB) to Ötztal-Bahnhof, then connect with regular VVT bus line 4194 (Ötztaler bus) running every half hour directly into central Sölden (stop Freizeit Arena or Postamt).

Tips

The exhibition galleries are completely step-free and fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers; all interactive stations feature informative multilingual signage in German and English. Plan approximately 1.5 to 2 hours for the tour. Combine your visit with the swimming and wellness facilities at Freizeit Arena Sölden or a mountain ascent to Gaislachkogl.
